items.title: Test function space d of an open set
items.strategy: Use the existing real multi-index convention componentwise for complex-valued tests; compact supports are contained in Omega.
items.statement: D(Omega)=C_c^infinity(Omega;C), Omega open in R^n, n>=1. Pairings are complex bilinear, with no conjugation.

items.title: Fixed support test function frechet space
items.strategy: Define the seminorm topology and displayed metric; completeness is proved in the following lemma rather than assumed from the name Frechet.
items.statement: D_K consists of tests supported in K compactly contained in Omega, with p_m=max_{|alpha|<=m} sup_K |partial^alpha phi|.

items.title: Test function topology
items.strategy: Define through the family of seminorms continuous on every D_K; the universal-property lemma proves existence and the topology claims. Do not define it by sequences.
items.statement: D carries the finest locally convex topology making each D_K inclusion continuous.

items.title: Distribution
items.strategy: Use actual LF continuity, not an unsupported sequence-only definition.
items.statement: A distribution is a continuous complex-linear functional D(Omega)->C.

items.title: Regular distribution from a locally integrable function
items.strategy: Absolute integrability holds on each compact support; continuity and injectivity are next.
items.statement: For f locally integrable, u_f(phi)=integral f phi.

items.title: Convolution of a distribution with a test function
items.strategy: Reflection accounts for signs; smoothness and continuity are proved next.
items.statement: On R^n set (u*phi)(x)=<u(y),phi(x-y)> for phi in D. On Omega use only x for which x-supp(phi) is contained in Omega.

items.title: Test function cutoffs and euclidean localization
items.statement: For compact K in an open Euclidean set Omega, construct chi in C_c^infinity(Omega), 0<=chi<=1, equal to one on a neighborhood of K. Every open cover of Omega has a countable locally finite smooth subordinate partition with compact supports.
items.strategy: Use the earlier Schwartz smooth-step cutoff construction for a nonnegative bump, normalize its integral, and convolve indicators of bounded neighborhoods with small bumps. For an open cover, use an exhaustion by compact distance-to-boundary sets and finitely many rational balls on each shell. Normalize the locally finite positive sum. Supply the shell-cover argument and all support margins; no appeal to the later manifold page. Countable constructions inherit at most DC; no sharper choice claim before closure audit.

items.title: Fixed support test function spaces are complete
items.statement: D_K is complete for d(f,g)=sum 2^(-m) min(1,p_m(f-g)). Its topology is the derivative-seminorm topology.
items.strategy: Take uniform limits of each derivative on all of R^n after zero extension. Integrating along coordinate segments identifies successive derivatives; all limits vanish outside K. This also handles compact K with empty interior.

items.title: Test function lf topology universal property
items.statement: The locally convex final topology exists, is Hausdorff, induces the prescribed topology on every D_K, is independent of compact exhaustion, and a linear map to a locally convex space is continuous iff each restriction to D_K is continuous.
items.strategy: Use all seminorms whose restrictions to each D_K are continuous. Global derivative sup seminorms separate points and recover the topology on each D_K. A seminorm composed with a candidate linear map proves the universal property; cofinality proves exhaustion independence. Prove continuity of vector operations directly from seminorm balls.

items.title: Test function operations are continuous
items.strategy: Control supports under each map and bound each derivative seminorm by finitely many source seminorms using chain and Leibniz rules. Treat parameter-dependent translation separately in the parameter lemma.
items.statement: Differentiation, multiplication by fixed a in C^infinity, translations between translated domains, and composition by a diffeomorphism are continuous on test spaces.

items.title: Local finite order characterization of distributions
items.strategy: Continuity on each seminorm space gives a finite intersection of neighborhoods; scale to a bound. Apply the LF universal property for the converse.
items.statement: u is a distribution iff for each compact K there are C_K and m_K with |u(phi)|<=C_K p_{m_K}(phi) on D_K.

items.title: Order of a distribution on a compact set
items.strategy: Separate compactwise order from the uniform order exponent. Arbitrary distributions may have unbounded orders along an exhaustion.
items.statement: Order on K is the least m with a bound on D_K (zero distribution assigned order 0); global finite order means one m works for every K, while constants may vary.

items.title: Distributional derivative
items.strategy: Continuous transpose of differentiation defines a distribution.
items.statement: partial^alpha u(phi)=(-1)^|alpha| u(partial^alpha phi).

items.title: Multiplication of a distribution by a smooth function
items.strategy: Use continuity of test multiplication; no product of arbitrary distributions is introduced.
items.statement: a u(phi)=u(a phi) for a smooth.

items.title: Leibniz rule for distributions
items.strategy: Prove first-order identity by testing and subtracting the derivative on a; iterate by the binomial recurrence.
items.statement: partial^alpha(a u)=sum_{beta<=alpha} binom(alpha,beta) (partial^beta a) partial^(alpha-beta)u.

items.title: Dirac delta and its derivatives
items.strategy: Evaluation and its derivatives obey fixed-support finite-order estimates.
items.statement: delta_a(phi)=phi(a); partial^alpha delta_a(phi)=(-1)^|alpha| partial^alpha phi(a).

items.title: Distributions form a sheaf
items.strategy: Restrictions use zero extension of tests. Define the glued value using a locally finite smooth partition; on any compact only finitely many summands occur, so continuity follows from finitely many finite-order bounds. Use refinements to establish independence.
items.statement: Compatible distributions on an arbitrary open cover glue uniquely.

items.title: Support of a distribution
items.strategy: The sheaf locality result proves the union of vanishing opens is itself a vanishing open. A test vanishing near support pairs to zero.
items.statement: Support is the complement of the largest open subset on which u vanishes.

items.title: Compactly supported distributions have global finite order
items.strategy: Insert chi=1 near support, apply the D_L estimate, and expand derivatives of chi phi. The bound concerns a compact neighborhood, not just the support itself.
items.statement: A compactly supported distribution admits |u(phi)|<=C max_{|alpha|<=m} sup_L |partial^alpha phi| for every test phi, with one compact neighborhood L of its support.

items.title: Distributions supported at one point
items.strategy: Taylor remainder and shrinking cutoffs show u kills every test whose finite jet at a vanishes. Factor through the finite jet space, and use cutoff monomials to identify coefficients. The zero combination has empty support, so do not assert support equals {a} without nonzero hypothesis.
items.statement: If supp(u) subset {a}, then u is a finite linear combination of derivatives of delta_a; conversely such combinations have support contained in {a}.

items.title: Bounded test function sets have common compact support
items.statement: B is bounded in D iff all its supports lie in a single compact K and sup_{f in B} p_m(f)<infinity for every m. Bounded means absorbed by every zero neighborhood.
items.strategy: If no K works, choose f_j in B and x_j escaping compact subsets with f_j(x_j) nonzero. The seminorm sup_j j |f(x_j)|/|f_j(x_j)| is finite and continuous on every D_K but unbounded on B. Then use global derivative seminorms. Convergent sequences plus their limits are bounded by finite-tail absorption.

items.title: Sequential convergence in test function space
items.strategy: Convergent sequences are bounded, hence have common compact support; use the induced D_K topology. Conversely the continuous inclusion carries D_K convergence to D.
items.statement: phi_j->phi in D iff the supports eventually lie in one compact K and every derivative converges uniformly.

items.title: Weak and strong topologies on distributions
items.strategy: Finite-order estimates and the bounded-set lemma show each strong seminorm is finite. Distinguish nets from sequences.
items.statement: Weak topology is generated by |u(phi)|; strong topology by sup_{phi in B}|u(phi)| for bounded B in D.

items.title: Locally integrable functions embed in distributions
items.strategy: Bound by ||f||_{L1(K)} p_0(phi). If all pairings vanish, local mollifications vanish; multiply by a cutoff and apply L1 approximate identities to obtain f=0 a.e. Bounded test sets give the continuity assertion.
items.statement: The map L1_loc(Omega)/a.e. -> D prime is injective and continuous for local L1 and strong distribution topologies.

items.title: Strong distribution convergence implies weak convergence
items.strategy: Every singleton test set is bounded. No unrestricted converse for nets is asserted.
items.statement: Strong convergence implies weak convergence.

items.title: Distributional differentiation is continuous and commutes
items.strategy: Commuting smooth partials gives commutation; integration by parts gives agreement. A continuous linear map sends bounded sets to bounded sets, so transpose continuity holds strongly as well as weakly.
items.statement: Distribution derivatives commute, extend classical derivatives, and are continuous in both weak and strong dual topologies.

items.title: Distribution pairing with smooth parameter families
items.statement: If F(x,y) is smooth and its y-support stays in a common compact set as x ranges over a compact subset, then x -> u(F(x,.)) is smooth and derivatives pass through u. Compact parameter integrals commute with u.
items.strategy: Taylor remainder estimates in every fixed-support seminorm give convergence of difference quotients; continuous functionals preserve those limits. Approximate compact integrals by Riemann sums in D_K, with all derivative errors controlled.

items.title: Convolution with a test function is smooth
items.strategy: On compact x-sets the y-tests have common compact support; apply the parameter lemma. The sign from reflection cancels the distribution derivative sign.
items.statement: u*phi is smooth on its domain and partial^alpha(u*phi)=(partial^alpha u)*phi=u*(partial^alpha phi).

items.title: Uniform finite order bounds for pointwise bounded distributions
items.statement: A pointwise bounded family of distributions has a common finite-order estimate on each D_K; every pointwise limit of distributions is a distribution.
items.strategy: Apply complete-metric Baire on D_K to the closed sets where every functional has modulus at most j. Subtract a ball from itself and scale to obtain the common seminorm estimate. Uses DC through Baire, not merely the normed-space uniform boundedness theorem.

items.title: Pullback of a distribution by a diffeomorphism
items.statement: For a smooth diffeomorphism F:U->V define <F^*u,phi>=<u,(phi/|det DF|) composed with F^{-1}>. Test functions use composition; distributions use the absolute Jacobian.
items.strategy: The support maps to a compact subset of V and all derivative seminorms obey chain/product estimates. Verify F^*u_f=u_{f composed with F} by change of variables; do not define pullback by arbitrary smooth maps.

items.title: Tensor product of distributions
items.statement: <u tensor v,Phi>=<u(x),<v(y),Phi(x,y)>> for compactly supported smooth Phi on U times V.
items.strategy: Parameter pairing gives a compactly supported smooth outer test function. This defines the candidate; continuity and pairing-order independence are established next.

items.title: Compactly supported distributions extend to smooth functions
items.statement: For compactly supported u, <u,f>=<u,chi f> defines a unique continuous extension to C^infinity, independent of chi=1 near supp(u).
items.strategy: The difference of two cutoff tests vanishes near the support; locality kills it. The finite-order bound gives continuity. Cutoff exhaustion converges in C^infinity, proving uniqueness without Hahn-Banach.

items.title: Sequential convergence of smooth multipliers and distributions
items.statement: If u_j->u weakly in D prime and a_j->a in C infinity on compact sets, then a_j u_j->a u weakly.
items.strategy: For a fixed test phi, all a_j phi lie in D_K and converge there; the common finite-order bound for u_j controls u_j((a_j-a)phi), and weak convergence controls (u_j-u)(a phi).

items.title: Extension by zero for distributions with ambient closed support
items.statement: If F is closed in R^n, F subset Omega open, and u in D prime(Omega) has support contained in F, then u extends uniquely to a distribution on R^n with support contained in F.
items.strategy: Glue u on Omega and zero on R^n minus F. They agree on the overlap. Ambient closedness is essential; do not promise extension across boundary for arbitrary distributions.

items.title: Translation invariant test function operators are convolutions
items.statement: A continuous linear map L:D(R^n)->C(R^n), with the compact-open topology on C, commuting with translations is convolution by a unique distribution. Its outputs are smooth.
items.strategy: Define u(phi)=(L(check phi))(0), which is continuous. Translation invariance gives Lphi(x)=u(phi(x-.)); smoothness follows from the convolution theorem. Conversely finite-order parameter estimates show u convolution is continuous D->C infinity.

items.title: Complex l one functionals on finite measure spaces have bounded densities
items.statement: A bounded complex-linear functional on complex L1 of a finite-measure space has a bounded complex density g representing it by integral f g.
items.strategy: Apply the real p=1 theorem to the real and imaginary parts of the functional restricted to real functions. Combine the two bounded real densities, then extend the identity by complex linearity. A bound of twice the original operator norm suffices; do not assume norm attainment.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis; provisional backing pending complete verification

items.title: Local structure of distributions as derivatives of continuous functions
items.strategy: Localize by a cutoff first and extend the compactly supported distribution to R^n; enclose its support in a box. Iterated FTC bounds p_m(phi) by C||partial_1^(m+1)...partial_n^(m+1)phi||_1. Extend the induced functional on that derivative image by complex Hahn-Banach, represent it by L infinity on the finite-measure box, and integrate once in each coordinate to obtain a continuous primitive. Do not assume arbitrary K itself is a cube. Inherits HB and the measure-theory choice costs. Apply the new complex L1 representation lemma: the published sigma-finite duality statement is real-valued.
items.statement: For each K compactly contained in Omega, u agrees on D_K with one finite mixed derivative of a continuous function on Omega.

items.title: Compact support continuous primitive representation
items.statement: If u has compact support K and order m, for K subset V open there are finitely many continuous g_beta supported in V with u=sum partial^beta g_beta; beta_j<=m+2 is sufficient.
items.strategy: Use a cutoff supported in a relatively compact neighborhood inside V; the local primitive representation and Leibniz expansion produce continuous coefficient functions with the required supports.

items.title: Global locally finite structure of distributions
items.strategy: Localize by a countable locally finite compact partition, apply the support-controlled primitive representation, and group equal multi-indices. Each compact meets finitely many local pieces and therefore finitely many orders. Uniform order bounds give one finite multi-index box. Record countable selection cost.
items.statement: Every distribution is a locally finite sum sum_alpha partial^alpha u_{g_alpha} of continuous functions; if its global order is finite, only finitely many multi-indices are needed.

items.title: Finite sums of product tests are dense on product open sets
items.statement: Every test on U times V is a D-limit of finite sums f_j(x)g_j(y), with all supports in one compact product.
items.strategy: Convolve with product unit-mass mollifiers of small radius; all derivatives converge uniformly with one compact support margin. Approximate the parameter integral by finite Riemann sums of separated kernels in every derivative seminorm. Diagonal choices give convergence in D. No distribution convolution or Fourier-series theorem is required.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis; provisional backing pending complete verification

items.title: Tensor product distributions and iterated pairings
items.statement: The tensor pairing is a distribution, has support supp(u) times supp(v), and is unchanged on exchanging the order of the pairings. Three-factor pairings associate.
items.strategy: Prove a mixed-derivative estimate on each product compact. Iterated pairings agree on separated tests; apply the product-test density lemma to pass to every test. Repeat in three blocks. Locality and products of local witnesses identify tensor support.

items.title: Convolution of distributions when one has compact support
items.strategy: Choose a cutoff equal to one near (supp u times supp v) intersect addition^{-1}(supp psi), which is compact under the stated support hypothesis.
items.statement: If at least one of u,v has compact support on R^n, define u*v on a test psi by the tensor pairing with a compact cutoff times psi(x+y).

items.title: Convolution of distributions is well defined under the support hypothesis
items.strategy: Compactness of the relevant intersection allows one cutoff per compact family of tests. Tensor support kills the cutoff difference; mixed derivative bounds give continuity. Closedness of the sum uses one compact summand.
items.statement: The convolution candidate is cutoff-independent, continuous on each D_K, commutative, and has support contained in supp(u)+supp(v).

items.title: Mollifier approximation in distributions
items.strategy: Test using reflected mollifier convolution. Supports stay in one compact neighborhood and all derivatives converge uniformly. For a global smooth approximating sequence use cutoffs along an exhaustion before mollifying.
items.statement: For u in D prime(Omega), local convolution with rho_epsilon converges weakly to u as epsilon tends to zero.

items.title: A distribution with zero derivatives on a connected open set is constant
items.strategy: Mollify on relatively compact balls: derivatives of the smooth mollifications vanish. Their constants converge by testing against a fixed unit-integral test. Pass to u and glue constants across overlapping balls using connectedness.
items.statement: If all first derivatives of u vanish on a connected nonempty open set, u equals one constant regular distribution; on a disconnected set constants may differ by component.

items.title: Smooth functions are weakly dense in distributions
items.strategy: Use exhaustion cutoffs chi_j equal to one on increasing compacts and radii epsilon_j tending to zero so chi_j u can be extended by zero and convolved globally. On any fixed compact the argument eventually reduces to the mollifier theorem.
items.statement: Smooth regular distributions are weakly dense in D prime(Omega).

items.title: Associativity of distribution convolution under compact support
items.strategy: Use a common compact cutoff in the three-variable pairing on each test support. Tensor pairing independence proves associativity; differentiation passes under pairing. Do not claim arbitrary pairwise existence guarantees associativity. A stronger properly-summing triple statement needs its explicit properness proof.
items.statement: For u,v,w with at least two compactly supported, (u*v)*w=u*(v*w); derivatives commute with permitted convolution. Also delta_0*u=u and (partial^alpha delta_0)*u=partial^alpha u.

items.title: Closed bounded test function sets are compact
items.statement: Every closed bounded subset of D(Omega) is compact.
items.strategy: Locate it in D_K; bounds on next derivatives give equicontinuity on a containing box after zero extension. Apply real Arzela-Ascoli separately to real and imaginary parts of every derivative, diagonally extract, and use derivative compatibility. Metric sequential compactness gives compactness in D_K and hence D. Retain inherited countable-selection assumptions.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis; provisional backing pending complete verification

title: Distributions Test Functions and Differentiation — Examples

items.title: Derivative of the heaviside function is dirac delta
items.strategy: Integrate -integral_0^infinity phi prime=phi(0); the assigned value at zero is immaterial.
items.statement: On R, H=1_(0,infinity) has H prime=delta_0.

items.title: Derivatives of piecewise smooth functions include jump deltas
items.strategy: Integrate by parts away from each break point, then use the finite one-sided limits and local integrability of g to pass to the endpoints. Only finitely many pieces meet a test support; C1 on open pieces alone does not guarantee that g defines a regular distribution.
items.statement: Let f be locally integrable and C1 between a locally finite set of break points, with finite one-sided values at each break point and locally integrable classical piecewise derivative g. Then Df=u_g+sum_a (f(a+)-f(a-))delta_a. In particular this applies when f is C1 up to each side of every break point.

items.title: Distributional laplacian of the newtonian kernel
items.strategy: Verify local integrability and harmonicity off zero. Integrate over the punctured domain; track the inward normal on the inner sphere and the limit of its flux. Requires a prior divergence/Green formula; unresolved source and dependency obligation F9-3.
items.statement: In R^3, Delta[-1/(4 pi |x|)]=delta_0.

items.title: Principal value distribution one over x
items.strategy: Subtract phi(0) on a fixed symmetric interval around zero; the mean value bound controls the integrand, while the compact tail is integrable.
items.statement: pv(1/x)(phi)=lim_{epsilon->0} integral_|x|>epsilon phi(x)/x dx exists and is a distribution.

items.title: Not every distribution is a locally integrable function
items.strategy: If represented by f, tests off zero imply f=0 a.e. off zero, hence a.e. everywhere; then delta_0 would vanish.
items.statement: delta_0 cannot be represented by a locally integrable function.

items.title: Pointwise convergent functions need not converge as distributions without local control
items.strategy: Take f_j(x)=j rho(jx-2) with rho supported in (-1/2,1/2), mass one. f_j(x)->0 for every x including zero, but pairing after substitution tends to phi(0).
items.statement: Pointwise convergence alone does not force distribution convergence to the same limit.

items.title: Compactly supported distributions have global finite order
items.strategy: Apply the A theorem and exhibit the direct derivative-evaluation bound; rescale cutoff monomials to exclude smaller order.
items.statement: For partial^alpha delta_a, the compact cutoff estimate has order |alpha|.

items.title: Sobolev weak derivatives belong to pde
items.strategy: Orientation only; this pair provides the distribution derivative definition without defining W^{k,p}.
items.statement: Sobolev spaces and weak-solution estimates are supplied by the PDE track.

title: Tempered Distributions and the Fourier Transform

items.title: Tempered distribution
items.strategy: Use seminorm topology, with continuity equivalent to sequential continuity because S is metrizable.
items.statement: S prime(R^n) is the continuous complex-linear dual of S(R^n), with bilinear distribution pairing.

items.title: Finite seminorm bound characterizes tempered distributions
items.strategy: A continuous functional is bounded on a finite intersection of seminorm balls; scale. Conversely the finite bound proves continuity.
items.statement: u is tempered iff |u(phi)|<=C max_{|alpha|<=N,|beta|<=M} sup_x |x^alpha partial^beta phi| for some C,N,M.

items.title: Weak and strong topologies on tempered distributions
items.strategy: The finite-seminorm bound makes the strong dual seminorms finite. Singleton bounded sets prove strong implies weak.
items.statement: Weak topology is pointwise on S; strong topology is uniform on bounded subsets of S, where bounded means bounded in every Schwartz seminorm.

items.title: Polynomial growth functions define tempered distributions
items.strategy: Bound the integral by the weighted L1 norm times a Schwartz seminorm. Use Holder with a sufficiently integrable inverse polynomial weight for Lp. Pointwise growth is sufficient, not a necessary characterization of regular tempered distributions. Include the radial calculation for |x|^p: local integrability at zero requires p>-n, and an inverse polynomial weight makes the tail integrable.
items.statement: If f is locally integrable and integral |f(x)|(1+|x|)^(-N) dx is finite for some N, it defines a tempered distribution. This includes polynomial growth outside a compact set and all Lp, 1<=p<=infinity.

items.title: Fourier transform of a tempered distribution
items.strategy: Transpose the Schwartz transform using the bilinear pairing; no complex conjugation or inverse transform in the defining pairing.
items.statement: Define <Fu,phi>=<u,Fphi> with Fphi(xi)=integral phi(x)exp(-2 pi i x.xi) dx.

items.title: Fourier transform on tempered distributions is well defined and continuous
items.strategy: Apply continuity on S, and bounded-set preservation for the strong dual.
items.statement: The Fourier transform on S prime is well-defined and continuous in weak and strong dual topologies.

items.title: Fourier transform is a topological automorphism of tempered distributions
items.strategy: Transpose the inverse and reflection identities from S directly, avoiding any reliance on unproved density of S in S prime.
items.statement: Fourier transform is an automorphism in both dual topologies; F^2 u=Ru, Ru(phi)=u(phi(-.)), and F^{-1}=RF.

items.title: Fourier transform agrees with l one and plancherel transforms
items.strategy: L1 agreement uses absolute Fubini. Approximate L2 functions by Schwartz functions, use Cauchy-Schwarz on each test pairing and the unitary extension, and pass to the limit.
items.statement: For f in L1, Fu_f=u_{integral Fourier f}; for f in L2, Fu_f=u_{Plancherel f}.

items.title: Convolution of a tempered distribution with a schwartz function
items.strategy: Translation and reflection keep the test Schwartz; this initially defines a scalar function.
items.statement: For u tempered and phi Schwartz define (u*phi)(x)=<u(y),phi(x-y)>.

items.title: Dirac comb
items.strategy: Choose decay order N>n and bound the sum by a weighted sup seminorm; on D the sum is locally finite.
items.statement: The Dirac comb III=sum_{k in Z^n} delta_k acts on Schwartz tests by their absolutely convergent lattice sum.

items.title: Dirac comb is fourier invariant
items.strategy: Pair with an arbitrary Schwartz test and apply the earlier A-page Poisson summation theorem, not its Gaussian B example.
items.statement: F III=III under the 2 pi normalization.

items.title: Test function inclusion in schwartz space is continuous
items.statement: The inclusion D(R^n)->S(R^n) is continuous with dense image.
items.strategy: On each D_K polynomial weights are bounded; use the LF universal property for continuity and the earlier Schwartz cutoff-density lemma for density. Density alone does not establish continuity.

items.title: Compactly supported distributions are tempered
items.strategy: Use the fixed cutoff and global finite-order estimate; uniqueness follows from D density in S. Compatibility with the D prime restriction is explicit.
items.statement: Every compactly supported distribution on R^n extends uniquely to a tempered distribution.

items.title: Tempered distributions embed continuously in distributions
items.strategy: Continuity of D->S sends bounded subsets to bounded subsets; transpose is continuous. Density makes the transpose injective. Do not claim a topological embedding onto its image.
items.statement: Restriction gives a continuous injection S prime->D prime for weak and strong topologies.

items.title: Smooth polynomially bounded multipliers on schwartz space
items.statement: If a is smooth and every derivative has some polynomial growth bound, multiplication by a is continuous S->S and hence on both dual topologies by transpose.
items.strategy: Expand derivatives by Leibniz and dominate each output seminorm by finitely many higher input seminorms. Polynomial multipliers and Schwartz multipliers are special cases; arbitrary smooth functions are not.

items.title: Differentiation and polynomial multiplication preserve tempered distributions
items.strategy: Transpose the corresponding continuous operators on S; send bounded sets to bounded sets for strong continuity.
items.statement: Differentiation and polynomial multiplication preserve S prime and are continuous weakly and strongly.

items.title: Fourier differentiation and multiplication identities on tempered distributions
items.strategy: Test each first-order identity and iterate, keeping the distribution derivative sign. Plane waves test the frequency sign.
items.statement: F(partial^alpha u)=(2 pi i xi)^alpha Fu and F(x^alpha u)=(-1/(2 pi i))^|alpha| partial_xi^alpha Fu.

items.title: Fourier transform of delta constants plane waves and polynomials
items.strategy: Evaluate the defining pairing at a; apply Schwartz inversion at zero; modulation and derivative identities give the remaining formulas.
items.statement: F delta_a=exp(-2 pi i a.xi), F1=delta_0, F exp(2 pi i b.x)=delta_b; F(partial^alpha delta_0)=(2 pi i xi)^alpha and F(x^alpha)=(-1/(2 pi i))^|alpha| partial^alpha delta_0.

items.title: Constant coefficient differential operators become polynomial multipliers
items.strategy: Use linearity and the derivative identity. Supply only algebraic equivalence, no general division, existence or regularity theorem.
items.statement: For P(partial)=sum a_alpha partial^alpha, F(P(partial)u)=P(2 pi i xi) Fu in S prime.

items.title: Schwartz parameter pairing and integral interchange
items.statement: Translations of a Schwartz test are smooth in every Schwartz seminorm. If all needed parameter integrals are dominated in every seminorm, a tempered distribution commutes with the integral.
items.strategy: Use Taylor integral remainders with polynomial weights; for integration approximate on compact parameter boxes by Riemann sums and control tails in every seminorm. State these estimates explicitly for each use, avoiding an unproved vector-valued integration theorem.

items.title: Tempered convolution is smooth with polynomial growth
items.strategy: Use the finite-seminorm bound on translated tests and weighted Taylor remainder convergence. Polynomial growth implies regular temperedness.
items.statement: u*phi is smooth, every derivative has polynomial growth, and partial^alpha(u*phi)=(partial^alpha u)*phi=u*(partial^alpha phi).

items.title: Fourier transform of a compactly supported distribution is a smooth multiplier
items.statement: For compactly supported v, Fv(xi)=<v(x),chi(x)exp(-2 pi i x.xi)> is smooth, independent of chi, and every derivative is polynomially bounded.
items.strategy: The compact finite-order estimate bounds every xi derivative by C_alpha(1+|xi|)^m. Commuting the compactly supported distribution pairing with the rapidly convergent Fourier integral identifies this function with Fv.

items.title: Compact distribution convolution preserves schwartz and tempered spaces
items.statement: If v has compact support then phi->v*phi maps S continuously to S. For u tempered, u*v is tempered and agrees with the D prime convolution.
items.strategy: Keep the compact support of v fixed and bound weighted derivatives of phi(x-y) uniformly over y in a compact neighborhood. Transpose the reflected convolution operator to S prime and check agreement on compactly supported tests.

items.title: Fourier transform converts allowed tempered convolutions to products
items.strategy: For the Schwartz case commute the pairing with a seminorm-dominated integral and use the Schwartz convolution identity. For compact support, Fv is a smooth multiplier and v preserves S under convolution; test and interchange the compact-support pairing. No product of two arbitrary distributions is used.
items.statement: F(u*phi)=(Fu)(Fphi) for u in S prime, phi in S; F(u*v)=(Fu)(Fv) for u in S prime and compactly supported v. Also F(phi u)=(Fphi)*(Fu).

title: Tempered Distributions and the Fourier Transform — Examples

items.title: Fourier transform of dirac and one
items.strategy: Evaluate against a Schwartz test and use inversion at zero.
items.statement: F delta_0=1 and F1=delta_0.

items.title: Fourier transform of a plane wave
items.strategy: Use modulation with the negative-sign Fourier transform.
items.statement: F exp(2 pi i b.x)=delta_b.

items.title: Fourier transform of delta derivatives and monomials
items.strategy: Compute the pairings including the minus sign in the derivative of delta.
items.statement: F(delta_0 prime)=2 pi i xi and Fx=-(2 pi i)^(-1)delta_0 prime on R.

items.title: Principal value one over x is tempered and its fourier transform
items.strategy: Reprove the principal-value bound on S directly so no B-page dependency is needed. Use x pv(1/x)=1 to get D Fpv=-2 pi i delta; derivative of sgn is 2 delta. The difference is constant and oddness forces zero; need continuity of reflection and the zero-derivative theorem.
items.statement: pv(1/x) is tempered and its Fourier transform is -i pi sgn(xi).

items.title: Dirac comb and poisson summation
items.strategy: Evaluate on a Gaussian and on a general Schwartz test; the latter is Poisson summation.
items.statement: The unit lattice comb is Fourier invariant.

items.title: Fundamental solution by division of a fourier symbol
items.strategy: Directly compute the integrable Fourier transform and multiply its symbol; Fourier injectivity proves the equation. This is a B example, not a PDE prerequisite.
items.statement: On R, E(x)=exp(-|x|)/2 satisfies (1-D^2)E=delta_0 and FE=1/(1+4 pi^2 xi^2).

items.title: Product of two distributions is not canonically defined
items.strategy: In the proposed algebra H^2=H implies 2H delta=delta; H^3=H gives 3H^2 delta=delta. Associativity yields delta=0, contradiction. This is a precisely stated obstruction, not a claim that no special distribution products exist.
items.statement: No associative commutative differential algebra extending all pointwise products of piecewise smooth functions can simultaneously retain the distribution derivative and an injective embedding of these distributions.

items.title: Convolution of two tempered distributions need not exist
items.strategy: The addition-pullback integral of a nonnegative test of positive mass diverges; the fibers have infinite volume. No claim is made about separately chosen regularizations.
items.statement: The ordinary convolution of the two tempered constant distributions 1 and 1 is undefined.

items.title: Paley wiener and microlocal analysis
items.strategy: Orientation only. No recorded unproved theorem is promoted to a supplier.
items.statement: Paley-Wiener theory and microlocal analysis lie beyond this foundational pair.
